## Overview
This method plots the breakdown of categorical data by cohorts in a bar plot. It includes some statistical testing for significance. It can be used to identify if a specific category of event is more or less common in a specific cohort.

## Method
This method compares the ratios of categories between cohorts. The statistical significance is computed using the chi square test.

## Considerations and Limitations
* Test results should not be interpreted, test is for demo purposes only (see Eleni)
* This has been designed for use with mutually exclusive categories such as sex or ethnicity

## Example
The following example shows how a value that can have one of two categorical values (`Cat 1` and `Cat 2`) can be explored.

This examples shows the following information:

1. In cohort A, approximately 2/3 of the patients are in `Cat 1` and 1/3 are in `Cat 2`.
1. In cohort B, the reverse is true. Approximately 1/3 of the patients are in `Cat 1` and 2/3 are in `Cat 2`.
1. The Pearson`s Chi-squared test has identified that these two cohorts are significantly different based on this variable (p-value < 0.01)

```{r, example, echo=FALSE, dpi=200, out.width="100%", fig.dim = c(8, 3)}

# Create a random sample of patients in two cohorts and assign random events
set.seed(123)
n <- 100
df_pde <- tibble::tibble(
  project_id = 1:n,
  cohort_id = project_id,
  cohort = sample(c("A","B"), n, replace = TRUE),
) %>%
dplyr::mutate(
  category = dplyr::if_else(
    cohort == "A",
    dplyr::if_else(runif(dplyr::n()) > 0.33, "Cat 1", "Cat 2"),
    dplyr::if_else(runif(dplyr::n()) > 0.66, "Cat 1", "Cat 2"),
  )
)

# Perform frequency analysis and get results
gcr <- gen_categorical_ratios(df_pde, "category", "cohort")
gcr$plt

```

`r gcr$test_res`
